biography.plain_text: Brian R. D'Isernia is an American shipbuilder who founded Eastern Shipbuilding Group after building vessels for his own commercial fishing fleet. D'Isernia retired from executive leadership in 2023 and became chairman emeritus.

long_biography.plain_text:
D'Isernia began his career as a New York lawyer, but commercial longline fishing drew him offshore. He assembled a four-vessel fishing enterprise and, dissatisfied with available construction, learned to design and specify boats for his own fleet. Demand from other operators turned that practical solution into a shipyard, established on Florida's Gulf Coast in 1976.

Eastern moved beyond fishing vessels into offshore supply ships, tugboats, towboats, ferries, research craft and patrol cutters. The company eventually operated three Gulf Coast yards and delivered more than 350 vessels. That breadth made D'Isernia's fortune a product of industrial shipbuilding rather than fishing alone. After more than five decades in maritime work, he handed the chairman and chief-executive roles to his son and became chairman emeritus.
